sources.entry: Upscayl - Free and open-source AI image upscaling tool. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/upscayl/upscayl) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: Upscayl is a free, open-source desktop app that uses AI (Real-ESRGAN models over Vulkan) to enlarge low-resolution images.
summary.what_it_does: Upscayl upscales low-resolution and pixelated images using AI models, guessing plausible detail to enlarge them. It is built on Real-ESRGAN and Vulkan, and the README says its backend is open source under AGPLv3. The README mentions a batch mode, post-processing steps (such as compression and scale selection) that run after upscaling for models that support them, and a GPU ID setting for choosing which GPU to use. A CLI named upscayl-ncnn is mentioned in the FAQ. The README says it cannot de-blur or fix out-of-focus images. Installers are offered for Linux (AppImage, RPM, DEB, ZIP, and Flatpak/Snap via distro stores), macOS 12+ (DMG or Homebrew cask), and Windows 10+ (EXE). Development uses npm with Node.js (recommended via Volta) and scripts for start, dist, and publish.
use_cases: Enlarge low-resolution photos without losing quality
Upscale pixelated or small images for printing or display
Batch upscale a folder of images
Sharpen and enhance old or low-res pictures
Run AI image upscaling from the command line
notable: Free and open-source AI image upscaler with a desktop GUI
Backend open source under AGPLv3, per the README
Ships a CLI tool called upscayl-ncnn
Supports custom and multiple models, including Remacri, UltraSharp, and High Fidelity, as credited in the README
caveats: Requires a Vulkan-compatible GPU; many integrated GPUs and CPUs do not work
Cannot de-blur or fix out-of-focus images
macOS and Windows installs may require extra security prompts (Gatekeeper/SmartScreen bypass steps in README)
